title: You’re Invited To Meet NYFW’s Next Generation Of Designers
text:
You’re Invited To Meet NYFW’s Next Generation Of Designers

When you look at the traditional New York Fashion Week calendar, the barriers to entry aren’t a secret. Between massive production budgets, rigid legacy structures, and steep venue costs, incredible independent talent is too often priced out of fashion’s biggest stage. That’s why this season, Refinery29 is officially teaming up with RAISEFashion to shift the narrative.

On September 11, we’re co-hosting The Penthouse Edit at The Standard, East Village. It’s a full-day, high-impact showcase designed to put fashion’s most exciting emerging designers directly in front of the industry’s top buyers, editors, stylists, and power players.

What’s even better? It’s open to the public, and you’re invited too. To secure your spot on the guest list, RSVP directly at the following link.

This isn’t just another presentation; it’s a dedicated platform for sustainable growth and real equity in fashion. We’re spotlighting the need-to-know names spanning ready-to-wear, luxury accessories, and fine jewelry. Each one is proof that the industry’s next era is being built on craft, community, and fresh perspectives.

Moving the needle in fashion requires capital, space, and access. We’re taking over the venue’s crown-jewel top floor alongside a group of partners who understand the importance of supporting independent talent.

Afterpay is stepping up in a major way for fashion’s next generation, co-hosting the event and dropping dedicated funding initiatives to fuel growth this season. Crown Royal is keeping the drinks flowing and awarding its own production grant during our VIP September 10th kickoff cocktail hour. (Bonus: You can shop the limited-edition Crown Royal x Juicy Couture capsule right on site, with proceeds going straight into the grant fund.) To top it off, we’re hosting an on-site shop featuring talent from Victoria’s Secret’s Runway to Revenue accelerator, giving you a chance to shop fashion’s next wave before everyone else.

Each of the names below is proof that the industry’s next era is being built on community. Get to know the designers shaping the next generation below, and stay tuned as we bring you exclusive insider coverage straight from The Penthouse Edit.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Almasika

Founded by Catherine Sarr, ALMASIKA transforms global heritage into a distinct language of fine jewelry. Drawing from years in the luxury diamond sector—including pivotal time at De Beers—Sarr leverages sculptural forms and noble materials to create symbolic, heirloom-quality pieces rooted in universal human connection.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Campillo

Designed by Patricio Campillo, Campillo reimagines traditional Mexican tailoring through a modern, artisanal lens. Deeply influenced by charrería culture and the rugged landscapes of Central Mexico, the brand fuses structured outerwear, raw leatherwork, and precise silhouettes to offer a fresh perspective on contemporary menswear and gender-fluid design.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Diarrablu

Created by Diarra Bousso, Diarrablu seamlessly bridges mathematical algorithms and West African craftsmanship. Designed and produced in Dakar, Senegal, the brand is celebrated for its conscious approach to resortwear, utilizing custom geometric prints, versatile wrap silhouettes, and sustainable production models that minimize waste.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Esenshel

Helmed by designer Eugene Taylor, Esenshel is a New York–based headwear and accessories brand redefining modern millinery. Known for its avant-garde proportions, fluid sculptural shapes, and architectural brims, the label challenges traditional hat-making techniques to deliver statement pieces that double as wearable art.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Gwen Beloti

Built on the principle of inclusive luxury, Gwen Beloti crafts timeless, accessible fine jewelry tailored for everyday wear. Based in New York, Beloti prioritizes precise sizing, high-quality gold-filled finishings, and minimalist silhouettes that elevate personal styling while celebrating self-expression.

DashDividers_1_500x100

K.ngsley

Founded by Kingsley Gbadegesin, K.NGSLEY is an activist-driven fashion brand known for its distinctive cut-out tanks, subverted basics, and body-conscious silhouettes. Rooted in Black, Queer, and Trans liberation, the label blends high-fashion construction with nightlife culture to create powerful, gender-inclusive ready-to-wear.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Le Blanc Studios

Co-founded by Angelo and Yamil Le Blanc, Le Blanc Studios is a Dominican-rooted streetwear and ready-to-wear label that channels Caribbean heritage into refined urban apparel. Blending military-inspired utility, historical narratives, and structural tailoring, the brand offers a sophisticated commentary on identity and movement.

DashDividers_1_500x100

McKenzie Liataud

Fine jewelry designer McKenzie Liautaud creates balance-minded, artisanal pieces that harmonize global travel with geometric elegance. Utilizing ethically sourced precious stones, pearls, and precious metals, Liautaud’s handcrafted talismans are designed to bring clarity, protection, and refined beauty to the modern collector.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Oleada

Co-founded by Tiffany Zhou and Tracy Luo, OLEADA designs functional luxury handbags for modern professional women. Combining architectural shapes with utilitarian features—such as laptop compartments, convertible straps, and durable recycled leathers—the brand crafts sleek, timeless leather goods engineered for modern travel and daily commutes.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Vontélle

Founded by Tracy Vontélle Green and Nikkia LeFevre, Vontélle creates bold, culturally inspired eyewear designed to fit broader facial structures and diverse bridge fits. Featuring vibrant African, Caribbean, and Latinx textiles embedded directly into handcrafted acetate frames, the brand delivers fashion-forward prescription and sunwear solutions.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Yesaet

Founded by Hswen Tesfamichael, Yesaet is an eco-conscious luxury label rooted in Ethiopian heritage and craft traditions. Made locally in New York using handwoven Ethiopian cottons and sustainable silk blends, the brand offers fluid, effortless silhouettes that celebrate slow fashion and generational craftsmanship.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Zut

Designed by Pierre-Antoine Vacheron, Zut is a contemporary accessories and footwear label recognized for its sculptural leathergoods and unconventional craftsmanship. Striking a balance between raw textures, architectural geometry, and Parisian elegance, Zut delivers subtle yet striking accents designed for the discerning minimalist.

title: ghd’s New Interactive Hair Styler Is So Impressive, I Ditched All My Old Hot Tools
text:
ghd’s New Interactive Hair Styler Is So Impressive, I Ditched All My Old Hot Tools

Like most of my journalist peers, I view AI with a healthy dose of antipathy. Call me a Luddite, but I don’t want my jewelry to tell me I’m not getting enough sleep or a bottle to scold me when I forget to drink water (it’s pretty often).

There are times, though, when I’ll gladly accept help from the machines, and one of them is taking the chore out of styling my hair. Happily, ghd seems to think it has cracked the code with its brand-new Sculpt Interactive Straightener.

ghd Sculpt Interactive Hair Straightener, $449

What is ghd Sculpt and what are the benefits?

Sculpt is ghd’s first-ever “interactive” styler. According to the brand, it’s “powered by AI that senses, learns and adapts to your hair’s temperature” — monitoring it 2,900 times per second, no less — “for personalized styling.” So, what exactly does that mean? Five times faster styling compared to the ghd Original straightener, better curl definition compared to the ghd Chronos straightener, and 2.5 times less frizz (but more on those later).

Perhaps the most impressive benefit, though, is no heat damage. Impossible, I hear you say! But it makes complete sense. The plates are packed with sensors that measure how much hair is between the plates, how quickly you’re going, and the angle at which you’re holding the tool. All of these factors send information to the sensors, which then decide how much heat you need and, more impressively, how much heat you don’t need. So instead of turning your straightener all the way up to a scorching 230° and keeping it there, the tool itself decides what your hair needs, minimizing damage such as split ends and color fade over time.

Of course, I’d always recommend using some form of heat protection. For me, that comes in the form of styling products, and I like Kérastase Elixir Ultime Hydrating Hair Oil, which not only moisturizes parched strands but also protects against heat and friction from styling.

What makes the ghd Sculpt Interactive Straightener special?

It was top London hairstylist Samantha Cusick who really convinced me, though. At the preview, I watched her conjure up a head full of waves on a model with thick hair worthy of a shampoo commercial in just five minutes flat — and it’s all down to the artfully designed plates.

“Infinity” plates, to be exact. Unlike the OG ghd straighteners, which have a sharp, clunky edge, these boast what the brand calls “waterfall” edges, so there are no seams per se, just a smooth surface all the way around. If you ask me, this makes the tool so ergonomic that, when it comes to creating waves, each section of hair appears to twirl itself into the plates, going in dead straight and coming out as a perfectly formed, almost accidentally perfect tousle — no snagging whatsoever.

Then there’s the shine. ghd promises 90% more versus naturally dried hair, and I can vouch for that. Each wave emerges from the plates with the kind of gloss usually only achieved using tools with dangerously high temperatures — what I thought I needed, since my hair is both thick and naturally curly.

What to know about ghd’s Sculpt Interactive Straightener:

• Personalizes temperature based on hair thickness, movement and styling angle, delivering more or less heat where needed for zero heat damage.

• Features slim “infinity” plates with smooth, waterfall edges, making light work of both straightening hair and creating waves.

• Promises 90% more shine, 2.5 times less frizz, and styles up to five times faster than the original ghd straightener.

DashDividers_1_500x100

How do you use ghd’s Sculpt Interactive Hair Straightener — and is it worth it?

It’s one thing watching an expert use a tool. The real proof was using it at home myself. While I consider myself something of a beauty expert, hairstyling always evades me, mainly because I’m impatient. Going slow with a straightener? I’m more of a ten-speedy-passes kind of person. Curling irons are a mystery to me, too, especially the ones with a clamp. With Sculpt, I can get pin-straight hair and two different types of wave — depending on which angle I hold the straightener — in moments, and it never feels like a chore.

To create a simple barrel-esque wave, I simply feed a section of hair into the plates from the mid-lengths, clamp down and twist the tool away from my face with both hands, pulling the hair through. Even better, I can save time by taking much larger sections of hair. Because these straighteners are so high-tech, the wave they create is just as perfect as when I feed through half the amount of hair with my ghd Chronos — the tool before Sculpt. When brushed, my hair looks professionally blown-out. I also love fashioning cool-girl S-waves by alternating the direction of the twist as I work down the section, creating a soft, undone bend. As for straightening, the plates feel slender and much easier to maneuver than my trusty ghd Chronos, making it easier to reach the roots and flatten frizz. Thanks to the temperature sensors, it takes fewer passes to make my curly hair straight, too.

Final thoughts

I was convinced that nothing could replace my ghd Chronos, but the Sculpt is smarter, niftier, and faster — and, for the first time, I actually don’t dread styling my hair in the morning. I’m also convinced that my hair is in better condition, too. It feels softer, springier and healthier, which could be thanks to the clever temperature control.

Where can you get ghd’s Sculpt Interactive Hair Straightener?

ghd’s Sculpt Interactive Hair Straightener retails for $499 and is available at ghd.com.

title: Nuance Nails Are The Creative Upgrade To The Clean Girl Manicure
text:
Nuance Nails Are The Creative Upgrade To The Clean Girl Manicure

If our favorite manicurists’ Instagram feeds are anything to go by, the “clean girl” manicure is officially on its way out. Taking its place? “Nuance nails”.

If, like us, you’ve been enamored with sheer pinks and barely-there nails (think OPI Bubble Bath and Essie Ballet Slippers), this is your sign to mix it up a little. Dreamed up by Japanese and Korean nail artists alike, this manicure trend is multifaceted. Think mismatched details, realistic marbling, color gradients, and nail art that mimics all manner of precious stones, from amethyst to emeralds.

What is the nuance nail trend?

Nail artist Emily Brady at Melting Mango Salon tells Refinery29 that this type of manicure looks best on a layered, translucent base — but anything goes. The beauty of the “nuance nail” manicure is that it doesn’t need to be perfect, and each nail can be totally different depending on your mood.

Instead of being tidy and identical, this manicure is certainly more cool-girl approved, hints Brady. “Nuance nails are a step up from the clean girl aesthetic,” she says. “They can still stay super neutral [if you want], but have something that adds a little sparkle to a ‘soap nail’ manicure.” She adds that there are quite a few layers, textures, and blending involved. For those who are still attached to the “clean nail” life, Brady thinks this is a more intricate alternative. “It allows [you] to elevate [your] everyday manicure without being too loud,” she explains.

title: The Future Of Young Hollywood Is Bright, Thanks To These Rising Stars
text:
The Future Of Young Hollywood Is Bright, Thanks To These Rising Stars

It’s a common misconception in Hollywood that instantaneous breakthroughs happen overnight. Academy Award winner Michael B. Jordan summed it up best a month before taking home the Oscar in March, telling Vanity Fair that the weirdest thing about Hollywood is that it “doesn’t glorify the hard work.” In other words, what looks like an overnight success is almost always the result of patience, preparation, and staying the course. The come-up deserves to be recognized. And Variety’s Power of Young Hollywood event last week did just that by celebrating the entertainment industry’s next generation of rising stars.

Held at the Four Seasons Hotel Los Angeles at Beverly Hills, the star-studded event honored Tyriq Withers with the New Leading Man Award; Tate McRae received the Triple Threat Award; Sombr was presented with the Songwriter of the Year Award; and Malachi Barton was recognized with the Rising Star Award.​

Year after year, Variety’s Power of Young Hollywood event remains an industry highlight, not only for gathering the best of promising young talent in one room but also for creating an exhilarating atmosphere that affirms creatives that their work has an impact. In an industry that’s quick to move on to the next new and promising face, Variety’s Power of Young Hollywood creates a space (even if it’s just for one swanky evening) for emerging actors, musicians, reality stars, and digital creators to pause and truly relish in their accomplishments. It’s a rare occasion for this business to celebrate the moment they’re in, but the sense of reflection was palpable throughout the night.

​While accepting his award, Withers shared that navigating the entertainment industry has come with its challenges, often taking shape in doubt and feelings of inadequacy.​

“For a long time, I didn’t feel like I deserved to be in places like this,” he said. “As an artist, I grew up believing that there would be some sort of endpoint. I get to the top of a mountain, but only to realize there’s many more mountains left after that.”​

The actor continued, “I thought I would wake up one day and feel like I had arrived. I believed I would stop doubting myself and finally be worthy of the opportunities that were in front of me. But it’s funny because it doesn’t really work like that. I think we all can agree on this. The truth is, I’ll never be ready. The only way to is through, and the best thing I can do is show up as the best version of me.”

​For the actor, receiving the New Leading Man Award has a double meaning. In the literal sense, Withers has graced the big screen starring in Reminders of Him (2026), Him (2025), and I Know What You Did Last Summer (2025). In July, Deadline announced that the Atlanta actor will star opposite Isabel May for the upcoming romantic comedy, Love Love. And while it’s every actor’s dream to play the lead across projects, Withers also sees that honor as a call to action for the type of person he wants to be not just in his professional life, but personal too.​

“If I want my career to stand for anything, I hope that it’s leading with love,” he continued. “This award says New Leading Man. I don’t get that as a title. I get that as a challenge –an invite, if you will. An invite to keep chasing and choosing stories that ask those different questions. An invite to keep collaborating with people who make me better. An invite, most importantly, to keep staying curious.”​

McRae, who recently headlined her first Lollapalooza drenched in liquid gold, was honored for being a triple threat poised for popstardom.​ Known for her high-production stage spectacles, the singer, dancer, and songwriter admitted that her over-the-top persona is her superpower.​

“I have a slight problem with doing the most at all times,” she said. “But honestly, I think that obsession has always been the thing that drives me. When I love something, I really love it. I want to know everything about it. I want to get better at it. I pretty much let it consume my entire life.”

​Singer-songwriter Sombr was recognized for dominating global airwaves and charts with his breakthrough smash hits such as “Back to Friends,” “Undressed,” and “12 to 12.” Before turning 21 in July, he hit major milestones that typically take many artists decades to reach.  ​

“I write all my songs alone in my bedroom, and to be recognized in this incredible setting is humbling,” he said. “Songwriting is the reason I’m alive. My mind can go to dark places, and it feels like the only thing I can turn to is writing songs.”​

He continued, “While songwriting is technically my job, it’s really my therapy and outlet. It’s my way of speaking when I don’t have the ability to do so any other way.​

From his debut album “I Barely Know Her” making the top 10 on the Billboard 100 to being Grammy-nominated for Best New Artist, the musician used his acceptance speech to thank his fans for making his career possible. He said, “I’d like to thank my fans because I would not be on this stage without them. I love my fans.”

​Malachi Barton rose to fame as a child actor, finding early success in shows like Stuck in the Middle, Instant Mom, and Henry Danger, among others. He’s set to star in the upcoming Disney threequel, Camp Rock 3. Despite growing up in the acting world, Barton knows greatness takes time and that it’s a journey that’ll be worth the wait.​

“I love that this award says Rising Star because you’re not done rising,” he said. “You’re still climbing. You’re still learning, taking risks, and getting better. That’s exactly how I feel.”

​Hosted by Mario Lopez and his son Dominic Luciano, the event also featured a live musical performance of “Pure” by British singer-songwriter Sienna Spiro.

title: The Total Solar Eclipse in Leo Is Here — & It’ll Change Your Life For Better Or Worse
text:
The Total Solar Eclipse in Leo Is Here — & It’ll Change Your Life For Better Or Worse

The first eclipse of the summer is here! The Total Solar Eclipse in Leo occurs on August 12th at 1:36 p.m Eastern Time, causing emotions to soar and the hands of fate to work overtime. If you’re lying beachside in northern Spain or cruising in Iceland, be sure to take cover because this intense lunation is changing our lives for better or worse.

Eclipses bring matters to light, as the moon moves between the sun and the Earth. They offer us a unique look at dynamics and situations, offering us the opportunity to grow. The focus of The Total Solar Eclipse in Leo is to look at our lives from a different perspective, recognizing that outdated belief systems or relationships need to evolve. Leo is a fixed sign, so moving toward a new path of consciousness is going to be challenging. The road we’ve been walking on is splitting into two different paths; it’s up to us to choose the one that connects with our own spirit. Before jumping into something shiny and exciting, take the time to make decisions by first weighing up the options. Eclipses make us feel like it’s now or never, and it’s not. Tempering our energy with rationality and pragmatism is the best way to proceed. 

The caveat is that we might not want to make changes; however, if we don’t do the work, then we will stay stagnant, or the universe will take the upper hand and transcend our lives for us, without our control. As you may have experienced in the past, the eclipses can be a little nasty if we’re not open to taking strides and a leap towards transformation. This eclipse in particular is close to the South Node of Destiny in Leo, so it’s forcing us to release what is no longer working in our lives.  

Fernando Salinas, tarot reader and author of The Joy of Tarot, explains: “Leo does not like being upstaged, and as it is ruled by the sun, a Total Solar Eclipse in Leo feels particularly tense. What does a show person do when the spotlight dims? How does a leader lead when they become invisible to their followers? This solar eclipse is occurring at a point in the sky that signifies a release of these expectations to be showy, and will help us all realize how we can shine without being seen and how sharing the limelight makes us all a little brighter. The Strength tarot card, which is associated with Leo, reminds us that compassion and grace are also ways of being strong, and this solar eclipse is going to help us put this into practice.” 

This eclipse comes into contact with Saturn retrograde in Aries. So, expect frustrations with authority, or those who are bossy, since we are resisting their domination and commands. Firmly leaning into our own power and being noncompliant with their projections encourages us to firm our own thoughts and beliefs, allowing us to evoke the positive nature of Leo. Simultaneously, we have to contemplate and activate the North Node of Destiny in Aquarius; this gives us a sense of altruism. We aren’t sitting idly by watching everything happen; we are taking action to defy the status quo and invigorate our lives.

Black Moon Lilith, as well as the asteroid Lilith, both of whom are in Sagittarius, and the asteroid Pallas in Aries, are firing up the energy. We want to be free and will do anything to fight for our independence. If that means cutting off people who are holding us back from being the truest versions of ourselves, then so be it. This isn’t an eclipse where we are hiding from reality; rather, we are confronting circumstances because we wish to shine and sparkle in our radiance. It’s about time people shower us with respect. It starts with the way we treat ourselves — the solar eclipse is a reminder of our fabulousness. 

There will be a moment of vexation because an ego death is happening; however, it doesn’t necessarily allude to an ongoing struggle in our lives, as long as we are releasing people and things that are not part of our journey. The destination may bring us back together with them, but it’s okay to part ways temporarily and to focus on ourselves.

title: Mars In Cancer Is Here — & You’ll Be Taken Out Of Your Comfort Zone
text:
Mars In Cancer Is Here — & You’ll Be Taken Out Of Your Comfort Zone

Watch out — this summer, the planets are still being messy. Mars’ dance in Cancer from August 11th to September 27th highlights honesty, nostalgia, and passive aggressiveness. We’re being taken out of our comfort zones as we stand up for what we believe in. 

Mars is considered to be in its “fall” when in Cancer, which means that the planet of aggression and action tends to behave indirectly rather than being confrontational. Mars in Cancer will find different ways to assert itself, veering from the norm. For example, this energy pushes us to flirt with our ex’s bestie instead of sending a text to get their attention. Also, Mars in Cancer alters its flow every few days, as the sign and phases of the moon (the planetary ruler of Cancer) are always evolving; it’s hard for us to be consistent.

Don’t be disheartened as there are some amazing attributes of Mars in Cancer. On a good day, Mars in Cancer genuinely cares for loved ones, offering protection and nurturing. This placement will go to extremes to help those it adores. History speaks louder than words, so Mars in Cancer defends those who share memories and are like family. The loyalty Mars in Cancer displays is like no other — especially when the chips are down for a friend or family member. Not forgetting that Mars in Cancer’s intuition is strong, prevailing in moments of uncertainty and confusion. All the more reason why it leads with its gut. 

This year, Mars’s cancer is going to bring an interesting mix our way. The transit starts with Mars aspecting the centaur Chiron on August 12th, which is retrograde in Taurus. At that moment, we are looking inward and how we can use our hearts to heal. On occasion, we may feel as though others have let us down, resulting in anger and defensiveness. There’s an opportunity to recover from the drama as long as we are gentle with ourselves and less critical, trusting in the process of mending situations. Keep in mind that this is a journey that is nonlinear and takes time. 

Then Neptune retrograde in Aries squares Mars in Cancer on August 17th, making us feel as though we are stuck in a moment. The caveat is that we are trying to make waves immediately, but the stars are causing stagnation. To deal with this energy, it’s best to stop in our tracks and to take the day off from willfully taking charge of matters. Instead of trying to fit a square peg through a circular hole, focus on self-care. Our dreams will happen tomorrow or sometime in the future, just maybe not on August 17th, so don’t take it personally if we’re told “no,” because this is just a chance for us to make changes and pour more passion into our visions. 

The most intense day of Mars’s dive in Cancer occurs on September 1st, when it aspects Saturn retrograde in Aries. Questions and issues with authority figures arise, such as who is the boss, because we want to be the one who makes the rules and rebels against the status quo. Being demanding isn’t going to help the situation, even though we think it will. The exact opposite is true — sometimes you have to play the game and slay them with kindness. The reason is that strategy is vital, giving us the motivation to steer the wheel in the way we please by having control over circumstances.

Mars in Cancer’s celestial swim finalizes with a fraught aspect to Chiron retrograde in Aries on September 27th. Again, there is the potential to work through issues; however, taking another look at the past may be triggering. Centering our focus on the relationship we have with ourselves could lead to accountability. Doing so is complicated because it means that we have to be aware of how we’ve hurt others and the role that we’ve had in situations. September 27th brings us face-to-face with our oppa, encouraging us to have the conversations to get the scoop on how to move forward and evolve. Yes, Mars in Cancer is going to be emotional and intense, but at the end of the transit, we may feel more compassion and empathy for ourselves and better understand how we can make improvements in our lives.

title: Your Horoscope This Week: August 9 To 15
text:
Your Horoscope This Week: August 9 To 15

Cosmic beings, welcome to eclipse season. This is one of the most astrologically active weeks of August, with the main event arriving on the 12th: the New Moon Total Solar Eclipse in Leo, the first Leo eclipse in over a decade. Solar eclipses accelerate new beginnings, and with this one taking place in bold, passionate, main-character Leo, you may already feel life pushing you toward a version of yourself that’s more confident, creative, visible, and willing to take risks. Opportunities can appear quickly, relationships can shift, and desires you’ve been sitting on may suddenly feel impossible to ignore. You don’t need to have a massive manifestation ritual planned either. Sometimes the eclipse is the intention, and what unfolds around you shows you exactly where this next six-month chapter wants to go.

The fiery energy is amplified by Mercury entering Leo on the 9th, making our communication more expressive, courageous, playful, and occasionally dramatic. We’re more willing to say what we mean, pitch the idea, flirt first, share the post, or admit that yes, we actually do want to be seen and celebrated. Then Mars enters Cancer on the 11th for six weeks, bringing sensitivity and domesticity into this otherwise fiery season. Our intuition gets stronger, home and family matters require more attention, and we may feel fiercely protective of the people and spaces that make us feel safe. Watch for moodiness, passive-aggressiveness, or acting from old emotional triggers when saying what you actually feel would save everyone a lot of time.

Ultimately, this is a week of rapid transformation that feels perfectly aligned with the Fire Horse energy of 2026. The Leo eclipse wants movement, courage, and enough self-trust to follow an opening even when you can’t predict exactly where it leads. Pay attention to what accelerates around the 12th rather than trying to control every detail of your fresh start. The next six months can radically transform the area of your life activated by this eclipse, and your job right now is to stay open enough to recognize when the universe has already started moving the pieces.

Read your horoscopes for your Sun and Rising signs for the most in-depth forecast.

DashDividers_1_500x100

Aries Sun & Rising:

Aries, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse is here to wake up the part of you that remembers life is supposed to feel exciting. Taking place on August 12th in your fate, fame, creativity, romance, and inner child sector, this is the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade, making it a major fresh-start portal for you. Something you create, launch, share, or courageously say yes to around this time could place you on an entirely different trajectory over the next six months. Romance can accelerate too, and you may suddenly feel ready to take a chance on someone or let yourself be pursued. Embody this eclipse by being bold enough to choose what brings you joy, even if you don’t have every step mapped out yet. Your inner child knows exactly what they want — let them have the mic.

Then Mars enters Cancer this week and begins a six-week journey through your home, family, and roots sector, bringing your attention back to your emotional foundation amidst all this eclipse excitement. You may suddenly want to move, renovate, spend more time at home, address a family situation, or become fiercely protective of your peace. Since Mars can get moody in Cancer, watch the tendency to snap at family members when you’ve actually been holding something in for three days. Say what you need, create the sanctuary you crave, and give yourself somewhere soft to land while your outer life starts accelerating.

Taurus Sun & Rising:

Taurus, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse could radically redefine what home means to you. The August 12th eclipse lands in your home, family, ancestry, and roots sector, and as the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade, it can initiate a major six-month chapter involving relocating, renovating, changing your family structure, or creating greater emotional security within yourself. You may realize that a living situation or family pattern you’ve grown accustomed to no longer fits who you’re becoming. Leo energy wants courage, so follow the vision that makes you feel more alive, even if it requires leaving your comfort zone. Your physical environment has a tremendous influence on your energy, and this eclipse could be the push you need to create a home that actually reflects your next era.

Mars enters Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks energizing your communication, learning, and local community sector, making you much more expressive about what you’re thinking and feeling. Writing, teaching, content creation, brainstorming, short trips, and important conversations can pick up considerably, and your intuition may help you communicate things that logic alone couldn’t articulate. Just watch your tone when emotions are running high, because Mars in Cancer can turn “I’m fine” into an entire psychological thriller. If something bothers you, address it before resentment writes the script for you.

Gemini Sun & Rising:

Gemini, your voice could take you somewhere completely unexpected during this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse. The eclipse takes place August 12th in your communication, learning, writing, and local community sector, opening a significant new chapter around how you express your ideas and how many people they can reach. Since this is the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade, a conversation, pitch, announcement, class, publication, social media project, or creative idea that emerges now could develop dramatically over the next six months. This is your invitation to communicate with more confidence and stop watering down an idea because you’re wondering how everyone else will receive it. Leo energy wants you to own the room, Gemini, and fortunately talking has never exactly been your problem.

Mars enters Cancer this week and begins a six-week transit through your money, security, and self-worth sector, increasing your motivation to earn more and create greater financial stability. You may feel inspired to launch another income stream, negotiate your rates, chase an overdue payment, or finally get more serious about where your money is going. Emotional spending can also increase under Mars in Cancer, though, especially when your version of self-care mysteriously keeps ending up in the shopping cart. Channel that urgency toward building the financial cushion you want, and let your actions reinforce the belief that your talents deserve to be properly compensated.

Cancer Sun & Rising:

Cancer, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse is opening a powerful new chapter around money, security, and how much you believe you deserve. Taking place on August 12th in your income and self-worth sector, the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade can accelerate changes around how you earn, spend, save, and value your own talents. A new income stream, offer, business idea, raise, or realization about what your time is worth could emerge around this eclipse and develop significantly over the next six months. Leo energy wants you to move with confidence, so this is your invitation to stop underestimating what you bring to the table. Let yourself want more, ask for more, and build the kind of financial security that allows you to breathe easier.

Then Mars enters your sign this week for six weeks, giving you a major boost of motivation, courage, and momentum. You may feel more decisive about what you want, more protective of your boundaries, and much less willing to sit around waiting for life to happen to you. Your emotions can also run hotter than usual, so give all that Mars energy somewhere productive to go through movement, creative projects, sex, work, or finally handling something you’ve been putting off. Watch the tendency to become defensive or take everything personally when you’re overstimulated. You’re entering a more action-oriented era, Cancer, and you get to decide where all that fire goes.

Leo Sun & Rising:

Leo, welcome to one of the biggest rebirths you’ve experienced in over a decade. The Total Solar Eclipse on August 12th takes place in your sign, opening a major six-month chapter around your identity, appearance, confidence, leadership, and personal direction. You may feel ready to reinvent yourself, launch something that places you in the spotlight, change how you look, take a major personal risk, or finally embody a version of yourself you’ve been envisioning for years. This eclipse is happening during your season, with Jupiter also in your sign, so there is tremendous momentum behind your expansion. Let yourself take up space. Let yourself be celebrated. You don’t need to know exactly where this new timeline leads before deciding that you’re ready for it.

Mars enters Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks in your spirituality, healing, and solitude sector, creating an interesting contrast to all this visibility. Your outer world may be accelerating while your body and spirit crave more sleep, privacy, reflection, and emotional processing behind the scenes. Old anger or unresolved feelings can resurface, particularly around family or situations you thought you were already over, so give yourself somewhere healthy to put them instead of letting them simmer. Protecting your energy will be just as important as pursuing opportunities. You can have your main-character moment and still turn your phone on Do Not Disturb.

Virgo Sun & Rising:

Virgo, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse is initiating a rebirth that most people may not even be able to see yet. Taking place August 12th in your spirituality, healing, subconscious, and solitude sector, the first Leo solar eclipse in over a decade can accelerate the release of fears, emotional baggage, self-sabotaging patterns, or chapters you’ve privately known were reaching their expiration date. Your intuition may be unusually loud through dreams, synchronicities, or sudden realizations, so give yourself enough quiet to actually hear it. The next six months are preparing you for a profound internal reset, and some of your greatest breakthroughs may come from giving yourself permission to rest, retreat, forgive, and stop carrying what has already served its purpose.

Mars enters Cancer this week and energizes your friendship, community, social media, and future-goals sector for the next six weeks, bringing much more movement into your social world. You may become motivated to collaborate, reconnect with friends, grow an online project, join a new community, or finally reach out to someone who could help move one of your dreams forward. You’ll also become more selective about who gets access to your energy, especially if certain friendships have felt one-sided or emotionally draining. Put effort into the relationships where care actually flows both ways, Virgo. The right community can help you accomplish much more than trying to figure everything out by yourself.

Libra Sun & Rising:

Libra, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse could introduce you to the people who are meant to play a major role in your next chapter. Taking place on August 12th in your friendship, community, social media, and future-goals sector, the first Leo Total Solar Eclipse in over a decade can rapidly expand your network and change how you think about the dreams you’re pursuing. A friendship, collaboration, online opportunity, or unexpected introduction could open a door that develops significantly over the next six months. Leo energy wants you to be seen, so show up, share what you’re working on, and stop assuming you have to accomplish everything alone. Your next breakthrough may come through someone who already sees the potential in you.

Mars enters Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks energizing your career and public image sector, making you considerably more ambitious about where you’re headed professionally. You may feel ready to pursue a promotion, launch something, take on more leadership, or finally make a move you’ve been contemplating behind the scenes. Since Cancer energy is emotional, you may also become more sensitive to recognition, criticism, or feeling overlooked at work, so watch the urge to take professional matters too personally. Put that energy into your craft and let your results speak for themselves. There’s plenty of momentum available if you know exactly where you want to direct it.

Scorpio Sun & Rising:

Scorpio, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse could catapult you into a completely different professional era. Taking place on August 12th in your career, reputation, and legacy sector, the first Leo Total Solar Eclipse in over a decade can bring a major launch, promotion, leadership opportunity, career pivot, or level of visibility that asks you to take yourself much more seriously. What begins now can develop dramatically over the next six months, especially if you’ve been preparing for something behind the scenes and wondering when your moment would arrive. Leo energy wants you out of hiding, Scorpio. Apply, pitch, launch, announce, lead, and let people know exactly what you’re capable of.

Mars enters fellow Water sign Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks energizing your travel, education, spirituality, publishing, and expansion sector, so you’re also craving a bigger world. You may suddenly become serious about booking an international trip, returning to school, teaching what you know, expanding a business, or pursuing an opportunity outside your usual environment. Your intuition can play a major role in deciding which direction to take, although Mars in Cancer can also make you defensive about your beliefs or convinced that your perspective is the only one that makes sense. Stay curious. The whole point of this transit is to discover what becomes possible once you venture beyond what you already know.

Sagittarius Sun & Rising:

Sagittarius, this week’s Leo Total Solar Eclipse is speaking your language: bigger dreams, bigger risks, and a much wider horizon. Taking place on August 12th in your travel, higher education, publishing, spirituality, and expansion sector, the first Leo Total Solar Eclipse in over a decade could accelerate a major move, international opportunity, educational journey, entrepreneurial vision, or decision to share your work with a much larger audience. Something that begins around this eclipse may radically expand your world over the next six months, so follow the opportunities that make you feel both excited and slightly intimidated. You’re naturally good at envisioning what else is possible; this eclipse wants you to actually go find out.

Mars enters Cancer this week and spends the next six weeks in your intimacy, transformation, and shared-resources sector, taking you into much deeper emotional territory. Money you share with others, debt, investments, outside funding, sex, trust, and energetic attachments may require more attention, and you could become motivated to finally deal with something you’ve been avoiding. There’s power in letting yourself merge with the right people while still knowing where your boundaries are.

You’re usually comfortable being the one with the plan, but this eclipse may show you how much further you can go when you allow the right people to invest in you, support you, and build alongside you.

Mars enters Cancer this week and begins a six-week journey through your health, work, and routine sector, giving you plenty of motivation to get your everyday life together. title: “I Would Move To Another Country”: Callum Turner & Monica Barbaro On One Night Only’s No Sex Mandate Premise
text:
“I Would Move To Another Country”: Callum Turner & Monica Barbaro On One Night Only’s No Sex Mandate Premise

When the trailer for One Night Only, Will Gluck’s new rom-com starring Monica Barbaro and Callum Turner, dropped, its absurd premise ignited a firestorm of debate across social media. In the movie, Allie (Barbaro) and Owen (Turner) play “two strangers [who] crash into each other in an ever-so-slightly fictionalized New York on the one night when single people are allowed to have sex,” as the official logline reads. The questions were immediate: How is the mandate enforced? What counts as sex in this sexless world? Why? How? What? The movie answers all of these questions (some more comprehensively than others) but the point is: One Night Only is a romantic comedy, emphasis on comedy. It’s supposed to be absurd. It’s supposed to make you laugh at the caricature portrayals of politicians who would enforce such archaic, puritanical beliefs. It’s close enough to reality — incels and tradwives alike are already pushing the anti-hookup culture agenda — that the jokes land. The premise is also just a purposely ludicrous backdrop to the love story. 

And Barbaro and Turner are so delightfully charming together that as you’re watching the film, the logistics and terrifyingly fascist implications of the aforementioned premise fade away and it becomes a fun, adventurous, flirtatious romp between two young, hot, horny singles. Try not to overthink it. When Refinery29 talked to the One Night Only stars in New York City before the film’s release, Barbaro and Turner were playful and at ease with each other, slipping easily into banter mirroring that of their characters, Allie and Owen. As Allie, Barbaro is engaging, slightly neurotic and relatably confident in one moment and insecure the next. As Owen, Turner is a solid leading man, delivering impeccable longing looks and yearning glances while also playing the faux bravado of a young man on the prowl perfectly. Together, they are a joy to watch. The pair are often in headlines for their dating lives (Turner just married mega pop star Dua Lipa and Barbaro is reportedly dating fellow actor Andrew Garfield), but their talent should stand on its own. They are both formidable romance leads. Here, the stars defend the movie’s controversial premise, make a case for getting serenaded on a date, and rattle off each other’s coffee and pizza orders without hesitation. 

The premise is so wild, but the movie grounds it in reality. There are —  terrifyingly — moments where I was like, “Oh, this could actually happen.” There’s a reference to incels, and as some of the politicians are speaking, it makes you think, “Wow, we’re maybe not too far off.” So, if this did happen in real life, how do you think it would go down?

Monica Barbaro: I think parts of this movie feel pretty familiar. I think it would feel like this really high-stress thing where everyone feels like they have to make the most of this one night, and maybe along the way forget about the more important deeper connections that can also [happen].

Callum Turner: The night’s kind of like New Year’s Eve, Halloween, Valentine’s Day, 4th of July, wrapped into one. 

MB: Chaos.

CT: It’s chaos. 

MB: And it’s that thing where, I feel like every New Year’s, I want to do something really nice, or Halloween, I’m like, I’m going to wear this, I’m going to do this costume, and I’m going to make it really fun. That happens in like early September, and then by the time it’s October 28th, I’m like, “Oh, shit. I have to find something in my drawer.” I would never be able to plan out my One Night Only well and then inevitably be disappointed. 

The movie sets up the disappointment, but it also sets up this anticipation and the buildup, and desperation that would come with a premise like this. One of the back and forths that I love between your characters is debating whether the buildup or the after is the best part of sex. Who are you with in that argument? 

CT: I think they’ve both got points. 

MB: I think they both have a solid case [laughs]. There are 365 days of the year, we’d be absolutely fine. Humans would be fine.

CT: As celibate?

MB: [laughs] I’m just saying the build up and the after both are great [but] I don’t believe in this mandate. I don’t think it should happen. Nobody accuse me of that, please. I would move to another country! 

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Refinery29 (@refinery29)

There are two different instances where Allie is being sung to on a date. In one, she is charmed by it. And in the other, she gets the ick. Do you think there’s ever an okay time to be sung to on a date?

MB: I think there’s always an okay time to be sung to. I think it’s more the lyrics of that particular song. 

CT: The first song you’re singing with him, too, right? 

MB: Yeah. He sings first and it’s lovely, and she sings along. One of my favorite lines in this whole movie is, “It’s not a duet.” It’s one of my favorite moments.

So, you’re all for being serenaded? 

MB: Yeah, it’s just that then if you turn the lyrics to something that I won’t say, that’s the end of that. 

CT: Now I have the lyrics in my head. 

MB: He has this thing where if you say a song, he has to start singing it. See, he’s sweating. 

CT: That one I’m not going to do. 

MB: We have to get a new song in his head. Um, Stand By Me! [laughs]

CT: I’m not going to do it. 

In the movie, it’s said that you don’t know somebody unless you know their pizza and their coffee orders. So, what are your pizza and coffee orders? 

CT: [Monica’s is] Cortado, oat milk. Margarita pizza, but if she’s feeling a little crazy, then she’ll throw everything on there. 

MB: Callum’s is a cappuccino, margarita pizza. 

CT: Oh, we know! 

MB: We said it like we’re really sad [but] we just locked in [laughs].

If you haven’t been keeping up on rom-coms, romance is back in a big way on TV and on film. Why do you think it left for a while and why do you think it’s back?

MB: I definitely think right now people need that catharsis. It’s kind of a wild time and even just like people trying to date in a big city, I think this movie feels cathartic for at least like friends of mine because I think they can see themselves in Allie and see that experience, like see those moments in dating where suddenly, “Oh, this turned. I got to get out of here.” Um and I think it’s just so fun to watch because of that. 

CT: And people love love. People love love! And watching people fall in love. And that’s what they get to do in this film.

One Night Only is in theaters now.

The Spider-Man: Brand New Day Kiss Everyone’s Talking About Is A Lesson In Consent

Spoilers ahead. There’s a moment in Spider-Man: Brand New Day where Peter Parker (Tom Holland) finally gets MJ (Zendaya) back… or so he thinks. After saving her from Jean Grey’s (Sadie Sink) clutches, MJ appears to remember who he is, and the pair share a loving kiss. Soon, it’s revealed that Jean is in MJ’s mind, and Peter’s ex still has no memory of him.

When Peter is eventually reunited with the real MJ, he apologizes and admits to kissing her while she wasn’t present. Although MJ has no memory of this, fans have latched onto how Peter’s apology is a good depiction of consent. For a superhero movie to break down stereotypes of toxic masculinity and show a character like Peter Parker embracing emotions and genuinely being a good guy, it’s somewhat refreshing.

Angelique Wan, co-founder and CEO of Consent Labs, tells Refinery29 the reason it’s resonated with so many people is that it feels familiar to many people. “The scene reflects the reality that harm is not always obvious or intentional, and that conversations about consent are rarely black and white. People don’t always have all the information they need to make fully informed choices,” she says.

Peter and MJ aren’t presented as ‘heroes’ or ‘villains’ in this kiss situation, because it’s a grey area. “These nuanced, everyday scenarios make the scene so relatable and open the door to meaningful conversations about consent. It’s also worth noting that the film doesn’t extend the same nuance to Jean Grey, who acted with full knowledge of the situation,” Wan adds.

On Threads, people have praised Spider-Man: Brand New Day for including the scene where Peter apologized to MJ. At no point does he dismiss or minimize her experience, and instead, he takes responsibility. “[This] reinforces that consent is ongoing and dynamic. Just because Peter and MJ were previously in a relationship doesn’t mean consent can be assumed,” Wan explains. “The wider storyline also highlights that consent depends on informed choice, reminding us that deception or withholding important information can undermine someone’s ability to give affirmative consent.”

The expert tells R29 that stories like this on the big screen (especially ones as popular as this) can demonstrate what accountability looks like in practice. Peter’s acknowledgment that his actions could have hurt someone else, regardless of intention, sends an important message about owning your mistakes. “By centring the experiences of those affected by our actions, we can take accountability and practice relational skills that cultivate healthier relationships,” she says. “It also encourages people to speak up when something doesn’t feel right and to think about how their own actions can affect others.”

While Spider-Man is fiction, the real-world lessons it teaches young people are very real. Whether it’s about consent, respect, or healthy communication, it helps start a conversation and makes the tough conversations less awkward.
